notes: Run each eval from evals/fixtures/glucose-companion unless 'cwd' says otherwise. The fixture has a PRD, an architecture doc, an ADR and design notes, no API contract, and a deliberate conflict (PRD: leave pairing any time; ADR 0003: cancelling mid-handshake locks the meter for 60 s). The fixture's architecture documents are Android-specific (Companion Device Manager), which the platform evals rely on.

evals.name: discovers-inputs-and-asks-for-confirmation
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding for this app.
expectations: Runs discover-inputs (or equivalent) and shows an availability table covering Spec, Architecture, Design and API
Lists docs/PRD.md as spec, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/adr/0003-ble-pairing.md as architecture, design/ux-notes.md as design
Marks API as missing and says how that will be handled (mock data derived from the spec, recorded as an assumption)
Reports the platform signals and suggests Android, citing ARCHITECTURE.md / ADR 0003 (Companion Device Manager), and asks the user to confirm the target platform instead of assuming both
Asks the user to confirm the inputs before proposing answers
Does not write any prototype HTML in this turn

evals.name: proposes-documented-answers-for-approval
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding. The docs in docs/ and design/ are authoritative; nothing else to add.
expectations: Presents a table of proposed answers taken from the documents, each with a source citation (file and section or fact ID)
Includes at least: primary users (adults with type 2 diabetes, many over 60), units (mmol/L), max 3 meters, skip-pairing option, brand colour #0B6E4F / Inter
Distinguishes documented (A) from inferred (B) answers, e.g. offline behaviour of the readings list is documented by ARCHITECTURE.md
Asks the user to approve all or correct by ID, and does not treat proposals as decided before approval
Mentions cosmetic defaults (class E) in one line rather than asking about them

evals.name: surfaces-the-conflict-as-a-question
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding. Docs are authoritative. I approve all the proposals you make from the documents.
expectations: Asks about the conflict between PRD 'leave pairing at any time' and ADR 0003 '60 s lock after cancelling mid-handshake', quoting both
Asks what the user sees during the 20–60 s initial sync and/or the 5–15 s handshake (architecture creates a UX question)
Asks about what happens when backend registration fails after pairing (partial success)
Asks no more than four questions in the round, each with options and a recommended option first
Does not ask about border radius, spacing, icon choice or other cosmetic details

evals.name: missing-spec-asks-for-description
evals.prompt: Make me a clickable prototype of a habit tracker app.
expectations: Reports that no spec, architecture or design documents were found
Asks for (or drafts from the prompt and asks to confirm) a short feature description: users, goal, main journey
Does not invent a full feature set and start building without confirmation

evals.name: playwright-mcp-missing
evals.setup: Run in an agent session with no Playwright MCP tools available.
evals.prompt: Prototype the meter pairing onboarding from the docs.
expectations: Notices that browser_navigate / browser_snapshot tools are not available
Runs check-playwright-mcp.mjs and shows the result
Asks for permission before running it with --configure
Explains that a session restart is needed and records it in prototype/notes/STATE.md
Continues with input discovery and clarifications instead of stopping
Does not silently use a different browser tool for verification

evals.name: verifies-with-playwright-mcp
evals.setup: Playwright MCP available; clarifications already answered in prototype/notes (prepare by running evals 1–3 to completion).
evals.prompt: Build and verify the prototype now.
expectations: Writes scenario files under prototype/scenarios/ with Given/When/Then before or alongside the screens
Serves the prototype with serve.mjs and drives it with Playwright MCP browser_* tools (resize, navigate, snapshot, click)
Exercises system back and runs window.__prototypeAudit()
Covers the permission-denied / Bluetooth-off path required by acceptance criterion 2
Saves screenshots under prototype/screenshots/android/<window>/<theme>/ and logs results in prototype/notes/VERIFICATION.md
Does not claim a scenario passes without a Playwright MCP run

evals.name: stops-at-handoff
evals.setup: Prototype verified; user has approved it.
expectations: Writes prototype/HANDOFF.md with screen inventory, navigation graph, per-screen state model, M3 component mapping, copy, decisions (assumptions listed first) and verification summary
Sets STATE.md to complete
Does not generate Jetpack Compose, Kotlin, SwiftUI or Swift code

evals.name: ios-target-with-android-architecture
evals.prompt: We're building the iPhone version now. Prototype the meter pairing onboarding for iOS.
expectations: Records the target platform as iOS from the user's instruction (P5), citing the prompt
Notices that ARCHITECTURE.md and ADR 0003 describe Android-specific pairing (Companion Device Manager) and asks how pairing works on iOS, rather than copying the Android behaviour
Plans the Bluetooth permission the iOS way: optional pre-prompt, one system alert with a purpose string, one denial is final with an Open Settings path
Scaffolds with --platform ios and follows references/platforms/ios/conventions.md (navigation bar back button and large titles, no FAB, alerts / action sheets, tab bar)
Plans verification at iphone 393×852 and iphone-se 375×667 (and ipad if in scope), with the largest Dynamic Type pass
Does not build Android screens or generate SwiftUI code

evals.name: verifies-both-platforms
evals.setup: Playwright MCP available; clarifications answered with P5 = both Android and iOS (prepare by running evals 1–3 and answering 'both').
evals.prompt: Build and verify the prototype now.
expectations: Scaffolds one prototype with --platform both and writes each screen once (no separate Android and iOS screen code)
Runs every journey on both platforms via ?platform=android and ?platform=ios, at the required windows for each (Android compact/medium/expanded, iOS iphone/iphone-se/ipad as scoped)
Checks back per platform, including the root: Android System back leaves the app; iOS back button or edge swipe, nothing at a tab's root
Covers the Bluetooth permission paths per platform: Android blocks after the second denial; iOS is blocked after one denial and offers Open Settings, with a purpose string
Saves screenshots under prototype/screenshots/android/… and prototype/screenshots/ios/…, and VERIFICATION.md has a Platform column
Treats a platform-foreign pattern (a FAB on iOS, an iOS-style back label on Android) as a major review finding

evals.name: handoff-both-platforms
evals.setup: Two-platform prototype verified; user has approved it.
expectations: HANDOFF.md has a component mapping for Android (Material 3) and for iOS (SwiftUI), marking components with no native equivalent (such as the undo toast) as custom
Lists the intended SF Symbol for each icon and each iOS permission purpose string in the copy section
Describes where navigation differs between the platforms (system back and leaving the app vs back button, edge swipe and modal Cancel)
Shows verification results per platform
Does not generate Compose, SwiftUI, Kotlin or Swift code

evals.name: should-not-trigger
evals.prompt: Fix the NullPointerException in DeviceRepository.kt when the meter disconnects.
expectations: Does not invoke the mobile-prototype skill
